findings.description: The inline IAM policy grants full wildcard access (ec2:*, s3:*, lambda:*, cloudwatch:*) on all resources ("Resource": "*") to the IAM user, violating least privilege and allowing the user (or anyone with its credentials) to perform virtually any action on these services.

Creating a long-lived IAM access key for a user rather than using temporary/assumed-role credentials increases the risk of credential leakage and provides a persistent, high-privilege secret tied to an overly permissive policy.

findings.issue_category: standing IAM user with programmatic access
findings.description: An IAM user is created with force_destroy enabled and an access key attached, combined with an excessively broad policy, creating a high-value credential target instead of using scoped roles or temporary credentials.

The output 'secret' exposes aws_iam_access_key.user.encrypted_secret, which along with the access key ID can allow reconstruction/use of long-lived AWS credentials; outputting secret-related values increases risk of credential leakage through state files, logs, or CI output.
